extensions.notes: Numeric/boolean typing through OAPIF: count=integer, ratio=numeric, active=logical. All seeded values round-trip with the declared types.

Temporal typing through OAPIF: created_at as POSIXct, event_date as Date, event_time as character. Instants are compared in UTC, so a lost timezone is a failure, not a class difference. All seeded temporal values round-trip.
JSON array columns through OAPIF/GeoJSON: tags as list, numbers as list; values tags=[red|blue] numbers=[0|1|2]. GeoJSON carries real arrays, so a stringified array would be a server-side typing bug.
Nullable `description`: 4 of 10 rows are NA (fixture seeds 4 NULLs); 'alpha' is NA and 'beta' is 'description_1'. A server that emitted "" or the string "null" would fail this.

Null-geometry handling: 10 row(s) returned with 1 empty geometry/geometries (fixture seeds 10 features, 9 with geometry); the null-geometry row 'lambda' is present. Dropping it or failing the read would be a server bug.

st_bbox() of the returned features (-122.49000 37.71000 -122.37000 37.79000) against the OAPIF declared extent (-122.50000 37.70000 -122.35000 37.84000): the data extent must lie inside the advertised extent, otherwise clients that zoom to the declared extent hide features.
WKB (st_as_binary) and WKT (st_as_text) round-trip of 9 server geometries: max coordinate deviation 0.000e+00 (WKB 0.000e+00, WKT 0.000e+00), threshold 1e-06.
sf::st_is_valid() over 9 server geometries: 9 valid, 0 invalid, 0 indeterminate.

OAPIF advertises CRS list {3857, 4326} for the certification layer; both the storage CRS (EPSG:4326) and the Web Mercator alternative (EPSG:3857) must be offered or R users cannot request a projected read.

Server-side reprojection to EPSG:3857 (http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3857) returned (-13635524.4273, 4538539.1534); PROJ 9.4.0 via sf::st_transform() computes (-13635524.4273, 4538539.1534); max deviation 0.0000 m, threshold 0.01 m.

Axis order: the default response is [-122.4900, 37.7100] with Content-Crs <http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84> (must be lon,lat CRS84 per RFC 7946) and crs=http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/4326 returns [37.7100, -122.4900] with Content-Crs <http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/4326>, i.e. lat,lon order. Part 2 allows the CRS's declared (lat,lon) order for EPSG:4326, but only a Content-Crs that names the CRS lets a client know to swap back; garbage in either position puts every R point in the wrong hemisphere.

bbox axis-order contract for OAPIF: the specified order (CRS84 lon,lat per Features Core) selected 3 feature(s) (expected 3), and the reversed order returned HTTP 400 with 0 feature(s) — a server that accepted both orders would be guessing, and a client cannot tell which guess it got.
Full paginated walk in pages of 3 over 5 request(s) collected 10 unique feature name(s) with 0 duplicate(s); the fixture seeds 10. A drifting page window would show up as a duplicate or a missing id.

Oversized page request (limit/COUNT=100000) returned HTTP 400 with n/a row(s). The server must clamp to its configured maximum or reject with a 4xx; a 5xx or an unbounded read is the bug this case looks for.
Paging counters on a 2-feature page (httr transport-shape check): numberMatched=10 (expected 10), numberReturned=2, actual features=2. numberMatched must be the unpaged total, not the page size.

Offset/startIndex past the end returned HTTP 200 with 0 feature(s) and numberMatched=10 (expected 200, 0 features, 10 matched). Wrapping around or erroring here breaks every client that walks to the end.

Zero-size page request (limit/COUNT=0) returned HTTP 400 with 0 feature(s): a structured 4xx or an empty 200 are both defensible; a 5xx or a full result set is not. Body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"limit must be 1 or greater.","instance":"/ogc/feature...

End-to-end GeoPackage fidelity: the OAPIF response was written with sf::st_write() and read back with sf::st_read() — 10/10 rows, names match, empty geometries match, max coordinate deviation 0.000e+00. (JSON array columns are flattened to text first: OGR refuses list columns.)

End-to-end GeoJSON fidelity: the OAPIF response was written with sf::st_write() and read back with sf::st_read() — 10/10 rows, names match, empty geometries match, max coordinate deviation 0.000e+00. (JSON array columns are flattened to text first: OGR refuses list columns.)

Advertised output formats all serve the complete feature set: f=json -> HTTP 200, 12833 byte(s), anchor present, last feature present; f=csv -> HTTP 200, 2111 byte(s), anchor present, last feature present; f=gml -> HTTP 200, 11023 byte(s), anchor present, last feature present.

404-vs-400 distinction: unknown collection 'does-not-exist-9999' returned 404 (expected 404) and a malformed `limit` returned 400 (expected 400). Collapsing both into one status makes client retry logic wrong.

Malformed CRS 'http://example.invalid/crs/nope' returned HTTP 400 with a structured error body (problem+json / ExceptionReport). A 500 or a silent fallback to the storage CRS would both be server bugs: the client would believe it received the CRS it asked for.

401 challenge shape on /api/v1/admin/services: WWW-Authenticate: ApiKey realm="Honua Admin", header="X-API-Key". The challenge must name the scheme and the header so a client can discover how to authenticate.
A wrong X-API-Key value returned HTTP 401 on /api/v1/admin/services; it must be 401 (bad credential), not 403 (authenticated but forbidden) and never 500.

GDAL_HTTP_HEADERS carried 'X-API-Key: <admin key>' through sf::st_layers() on the OAPIF DSN: 5 layer(s) listed and the certification target '0' is present. Proves the credential path works through the sf/GDAL stack, not just httr.

Cross-protocol extent agreement: OGC API Features collection extent [-122.50000 37.70000 -122.35000 37.84000] vs WFS ows:WGS84BoundingBox [-122.50000 37.70000 -122.35000 37.84000]; max deviation 0.000e+00. Disagreement means a client that zooms by metadata sees a different map depending on the protocol.
Cross-protocol count agreement: OGC API Features numberMatched=10, WFS resultType=hits numberMatched=10, fixture total=10.
Cross-protocol CRS agreement: OGC API Features offers {3857, 4326}, WFS offers {3857, 4326}. A CRS available on one protocol but not the other is a metadata bug, not a capability difference.

Cross-protocol attribute agreement: 13 field(s) in OGC API Features items vs 13 in WFS DescribeFeatureType. WFS-only: {}. OAPIF-only: {}. The same layer must expose the same attributes on both protocols.

Landing page http://honua:5000/ogc/features returned HTTP 200 with link relations {self, alternate, service-desc, conformance, data, https://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/map, http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/tilesets-vector}. OGC API Features Core requires self, service-desc/service-doc, conformance and data.
Declared-vs-honoured conformance: 7 of 26 declared classes were probed and all held. A conformance class the server declares but does not implement is a server bug.

Link relations: self=http://honua:5000/ogc/features/collections/0/items?limit=3; following `next` returned HTTP 200 with 3 feature(s) disjoint from page one (overlap 0); the final page advertises relations {self, alternate, prev, http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/queryables} and must not advertise `next`.
Single-item retrieval /items/1 returned HTTP 200 as a GeoJSON Feature with name 'alpha' (expected the 'alpha' anchor). Item ids advertised in the collection must be addressable.

datetime=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z/2024-01-03T00:00:00Z returned HTTP 200 with 2 of 10 feature(s); every returned created_at is inside the interval. A datetime filter that returns everything is not a filter.
CQL2-text `filter=status = 'active'` returned HTTP 200 with 5 feature(s) (expected 5) and status values {active}. This is the protocol filter parameter, not a client-side filter.
